exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs vaginal delivery)
cohort: 41 preterm infants born at 25-30 weeks gestation with birth weights between 430-990 g
finding: The mode of delivery influences the initial intestinal microbiome composition of preterm infants, but infant weight at the time of sampling is a better predictor of microbiome development than postconceptional age.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was associated with a higher abundance of Staphylococcus, while vaginal delivery was associated with higher abundance of Escherichia and Bacteroides.
